calibration.calibration_regime_meaning: B (direct effects only): damage curves are read as each agent's direct dependency, interaction edges add the indirect part

parameters.name: model.trophic_transfer_efficiency
parameters.note: Midpoint of the 5-20% energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels (the textbook range following Lindeman 1942; from memory, verify). The midpoint is a choice, not a measurement.

parameters.name: model.trophic_amplification_exponent
parameters.note: No source: damps the pyramid ratio to 1.6-4.1× amplification for trophic levels 1-3.

parameters.name: model.keystone_edge_multiplier
parameters.note: No source: outgoing edge strengths of a collapsed keystone agent are multiplied by this factor.

parameters.name: carbon_price.year0
parameters.note: Social cost of carbon. The 2020-emissions value is used as the year-0 price: EPA's own path gives about $215 for 2026 emissions, so year-0 carbon damage is understated by about 13%. 2020 euros, no inflation adjustment.
parameters.source: US EPA (2023), Report on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases, Table ES.1: $190/tCO2 (2020 emissions, 2020 USD, 2% near-term rate), at the ECB 2020 average rate of 1.1422 USD/EUR

parameters.name: carbon_price.growth
parameters.note: 60-year average of a decelerating path (1.6%/yr in 2020-2050, 1.2%/yr in 2030-2080).

parameters.name: resource.area_ha
parameters.note: Units / reference density of 400 trees/ha. Terra firme, DBH >= 10 cm: ~400-600 stems/ha, stated without a citation; sets the per-tree carbon.

parameters.name: resource.unit_value
parameters.note: Selective-logging revenue per tree (one-off); no market source.
parameters.source: case author's choice ('Calibrated' in the docstring)

parameters.name: resource.safe_threshold_ratio
parameters.note: A basin-scale tipping point applied to a 1,000 ha patch, a scale mismatch (audit S4); under the area_loss damage model (Step 8d.1) the depletion beyond which the REMAINING resource starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs its average value.
parameters.source: Lovejoy & Nobre (2018): Amazon tipping point at 20-25% deforestation (via AMAZON_FOREST.md §6)

parameters.name: agents.annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Every agent; the dependency weights split it. The anchors' sources are partly unverified (web pages and authorless citations in the literature review, audit S4). For scale, de Groot et al. (2012): tropical forest Int$5,264/ha/yr, of which climate regulation Int$2,044.
parameters.source: sum of the non-carbon anchors of AMAZON_FOREST.md §8 for 1,000 ha: water cycling €150k, fisheries €20k, biodiversity/habitat €410k (Brouwer et al. 2022 meta-analysis, $410/ha/yr)

parameters.name: damage.threshold_logistic_steepness
parameters.note: Degradation of the REMAINING resource past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1, as for Posidonia): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span, the same curve for every agent. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. Not fitted to field data (calibration regime B). Monte Carlo range 6-18, uniform (Step 8e.4, as Posidonia: a judgement; the placeholder x/÷3 gave 4-36).

parameters.name: agent[Mycorrhizal Fungi].keystone_threshold

parameters.name: agent[Pollinators].keystone_threshold

parameters.name: edge[Mycorrhizal Fungi → Canopy Trees].strength

Monte Carlo range (Step 8e.4): x0.5 to x1.004. The incoming strengths into Canopy Trees sum to 0.996 of the in-degree cap of 1 (keystone boosts included), so the edges into it can rise only by x1.004 together before a draw breaks the cap; their documented values are therefore the top of their range (x1.004), not its middle. pricing.note: EXPERIMENTAL (decision D4, C8): endogenous pricing is quarantined. Every price is certified convergent (a run that cannot be certified fails instead of falling back to static values), but the formulation counts upstream value once per dependent agent and prices the whole loss at the end-state scarcity price, and most shipped anchors are placeholders. Do not use these figures as estimates.
